original_record.question: Which of the following can be deduced from the passage?

options.A: the writer believes that most Nigerians do not die natural deaths
options.B: obituaries insinuate that most Nigerians do not die natural deaths
options.C: the writer is convinced that every death in Nigeria is a big blow to the bereaved
options.D: the writer suspects that every death in Nigeria is a big blow to the bereaved

candidate.subject: english
candidate.question: Which of the following can be deduced from the passage?

options.A: the writer believes that most Nigerians do not die natural deaths
options.B: obituaries insinuate that most Nigerians do not die natural deaths
options.C: the writer is convinced that every death in Nigeria is a big blow to the bereaved
options.D: the writer suspects that every death in Nigeria is a big blow to the bereaved

candidate.explanation: The writer attributes the suggestion of unnatural deaths to obituary language and its praise of the deceased. This distinguishes what the notices imply from what the writer personally believes.
candidate.ai_explanation: The writer attributes the suggestion of unnatural deaths to obituary language and its praise of the deceased. This distinguishes what the notices imply from what the writer personally believes.
candidate.passage: There are one or two things this country can teach others, one of which is the art of writing obituaries. One suspects that the reason why some of our newspapers still manage to break even is because of the great amount of revenue they derive from obituaries. It is not unusual for about one quarter of the volume of an average daily to be constituted of obituaries and in memoriam alone. One possible explanation for this, it has been argued, is that Nigerians value their dead greatly. And there is a saying amongst us that you do not say evil things against the dead. This is obviously the philosophy behind the large dose of encomiums with which our dead are bestowed. From the evidences of these obituaries and In memoriam, every dead Nigerian must have been something of a saint while alive. This would explain why the death of most Nigerians is attributed to the evil machinations of the wicked. Only very few people in our country die natural death, and even when they do, the obituaries etc. always give the impression that such deaths constitute the saddest loss to befall the deceased’s family. And that is why writers of these obituaries and their allied advertisements are experts on ‘mortuary stylistics’. This ‘mortuary stylistics’, the study in the art of eulogizing the dead and making their loss sound so heart breaking, is one of the commodities we can export to other countries.

candidate.subject: english
candidate.question: The writer of the passage believes that delinquency laws are

options.A: not relevant to human society
options.B: only fit for young people
options.C: unfair to the juveniles
options.D: very fair to the adult world

candidate.explanation: The writer calls these laws a weapon directed by adults against young people and associates them with pride and intolerance. That language presents them as unfair to juveniles, not as neutral protection.
candidate.ai_explanation: The writer calls these laws a weapon directed by adults against young people and associates them with pride and intolerance. That language presents them as unfair to juveniles, not as neutral protection.
candidate.passage: Delinquency describes actions that would not be crimes if performed by adults. If a young person performs one of such actions then he has committed a crime. Delinquency is one of several status offences – offences that can be committed only by people in particular stations of life as determined by age, profession or a person’s role in society. For young people such offences include drinking, driving and smoking under age. Usually they are offences only to the extent that they help to preserve some of the good things of life for the exclusive enjoyment of the adult world. Delinquency is therefore a weapon forged in adult minds and directed by adult hands against young people. It is born out of envy, adult pride and intolerance. If the world changed overnight and the responsibility to make and enforce laws fell on juvenile shoulders, the adults should expect a raw deal in return. Delinquency would then certainly refer only to many of the adult actions now freely committed by them.

original_record.subject: english
original_record.question: According to the passage, Ludo is

options.A: more a game of skill than of chance
options.B: more a game of luck that of skill
options.C: equally a game of chance and skill
options.D: a game entirely of luck.

candidate.subject: english
candidate.question: According to the passage, Ludo is

options.A: more a game of skill than of chance
options.B: more a game of luck than of skill
options.C: equally a game of chance and skill
options.D: a game entirely of luck.

candidate.explanation: The passage recognises both skill and chance but explicitly calls luck dominant. It explains that persistent low throws can defeat even a skilful player, so luck has the greater role.
candidate.ai_explanation: The passage recognises both skill and chance but explicitly calls luck dominant. It explains that persistent low throws can defeat even a skilful player, so luck has the greater role.
candidate.passage: Those who are familiar with it will tell you that Ludo, like human life itself, is a game both of chance and skill. You need skill in deciding how to make the most advantageous use of the figures that turn up on the die when you cast it. Since each player has at least four alternative ways of using his figures, two players with equal luck may fare differently, depending on how cleverly each one uses his figures. The element of luck, again as in human life, plays a dominant role however. For no matter how skilful a player may be in using the figures he gets on the die, he has a slim chance of winning if he continually throws low figures. While a combination of ones and twos may be useful in checking the advance of one’s opponents, it will not take one home fast enough to win. On the other hand, consistent throws of sixes and fives, with even the very minimum of skill, will help a player to home all his four counters before any of the three other players, unless, of course, he has no idea of the game at all.
